statement: Choose a non-empty contiguous block of nums and sum it. Return the largest sum any such block can have.
reference:
def max_subarray(nums):
    best = nums[0]
    current = nums[0]
    for value in nums[1:]:
        current = max(value, current + value)
        best = max(best, current)
    return best

def max_subarray(nums):

statement: Two singly linked lists arrive serialized head-to-tail as integer arrays, each already in non-decreasing order. Splice their values into one serialized sorted array: at every step take the smaller of the two available front values, either one on a tie, until both lists are exhausted.
constraints: Each list is serialized as a JSON array of its node values from head to tail; no node objects appear.
Both inputs are non-decreasing; equal values are allowed
reference:
def merge_sorted(first, second):
    i = 0
    j = 0
    out = []
    while i < len(first) and j < len(second):
        if first[i] <= second[j]:
            out.append(first[i])
            i += 1
        else:
            out.append(second[j])
            j += 1
    out.extend(first[i:])
    out.extend(second[j:])
    return out

provenance.notes: The problem idea is the classic merge-two-sorted-lists exercise. The statement wording, head-to-tail array serialization, examples, hidden tests, reference and mutant were written originally for Pacio; no third-party text was copied.

statement: The array head serializes a singly linked list v1 ... vn from head to tail. Return the serialized list after the pass; when n is odd the originally middle value lands last.
constraints: The list is serialized as a JSON array of node values from head to tail.
For the split, the front half holds ceil(n/2) nodes; the back half is taken from the tail backwards.

statement: A singly linked list that may loop is stored as two parallel arrays: values[i] is the payload of node i, and links[i] is the array index of node i's successor, or -1 when node i has no successor. Traversal starts at node 0 and follows successor indices. Decide whether the walk ever arrives at a node it has already visited - in other words, whether following links from node 0 can loop forever.
constraints: 0 <= len(values) == len(links) <= 200; empty arrays describe the empty list.
Each links[i] is -1 or an index in 0..len(links)-1.
Node 0 is the head and every node is reachable from it, so the shape is exactly one walk that either stops at -1 or closes a single loop.
A plain value array cannot express a loop, hence the explicit index links.
edge_cases: loop that returns to the head
maximum length, with and without a loop

statement: Two non-negative integers live in singly linked lists written in reverse decimal order: the head node carries the ones digit and each later node carries the next power of ten. Add them digit by digit with carries, exactly as a columnar addition, and return the sum serialized as a reverse-order digit list. The result must not gain a spurious leading-zero node.
constraints: Each number is a JSON array of its decimal digits, least significant digit first.
The value zero is written as [0]; other arrays never end in a zero digit.
reference:
def add_two_numbers(left, right):
    carry = 0
    out = []
    index = 0
    while index < len(left) or index < len(right) or carry:
        x = left[index] if index < len(left) else 0
        y = right[index] if index < len(right) else 0
        total = x + y + carry
        out.append(total % 10)
        carry = total // 10
        index += 1
    return out

statement: Read the nested-triple tree level by level, exactly as flood water would: start with the root alone, then every level lists the children of the previous level from left to right. Return a list whose i-th row holds the values at depth i, root at row 0. The empty tree yields no rows.

Rows are ordered left to right and levels are ordered top to bottom; this ordering is part of the expected output.

statement: Using the nested-triple encoding, decide whether the tree honours the strict search-tree contract at every node: a node must sit above every lower bound inherited from its ancestors and below every upper bound inherited from its ancestors, not merely be well-ordered against its direct parent. Two equal values anywhere in the tree destroy validity.
constraints: A tree is encoded as nested JSON: null is the empty tree and every present node is the three-slot list [value, left, right]; a leaf is written [value, null, null].
Ordering is strict: left subtree values < node value < right subtree values must hold for every node and every descendant of that node.
